scope: first-pass verse-specific screening; unpublished, not comprehensive
methodology: Read Nehemiah 4:16–18 and Ezekiel 18:21–32 in ESV English, compared to Qur'an passage themes. No Hebrew critical text or manuscript collation. No direct dependence claims; other ayat classified provisionally, not proven to lack parallels.

verses.summary: Travel prayer concession when fearing attack; compare ritual-law context, not assume equivalence
Prayer under threat: alternating groups, weapons and vigilance; distinctive ritual arrangement
Prayer after danger: remembrance and prescribed prayer times
Revelation and just judgment; prohibition on advocacy for treacherous parties
Do not defend those who betray themselves
Concealed wrongdoing and human shame contrasted with divine knowledge
Advocacy in worldly life cannot secure acquittal before God
Wrongdoing followed by seeking forgiveness and divine mercy

staged_candidates.relationship: loose contrast: armed vigilance under threat
staged_candidates.shared: Groups organize armed vigilance during an ongoing task.
staged_candidates.differs: Nehemiah concerns rebuilding Jerusalem's wall with weapons and guards; Qur'an 4:102 prescribes alternating groups during congregational prayer and weapon readiness.
staged_candidates.verification: English ESV text read; Hebrew critical text and witness history not checked. Not a prayer-law parallel.

staged_candidates.relationship: thematic theological comparison: repentance and mercy
staged_candidates.shared: Both emphasize a path from wrongdoing to divine mercy or life through repentance.
staged_candidates.differs: Ezekiel addresses turning from wickedness and doing justice in a prophetic exhortation to Israel; Qur'an 4:110 emphasizes wrongdoing and seeking God's forgiveness, without Ezekiel's detailed life/death framing.
staged_candidates.verification: English ESV text read; Hebrew critical edition and manuscript witnesses not checked. Generic motif, not literary dependence.
